section.title: Generate the manual
section.para: The manual uses the DocBook Maven Plugin, matching the established OpenNLP manual toolchain. These are build plugins and do not become application dependencies.
Generate the HTML and PDF manual:

Open opennlp-addons-docs/target/docbkx/html/opennlp-addons.html in a browser. The PDF is written to opennlp-addons-docs/target/docbkx/pdf/opennlp-addons.pdf. Use a clean build after changing manual sources:

section.title: Maven publication
section.para: Each module uses the org.apache.opennlp.addons Maven group. The ASF parent POM supplies the Apache staging repository (apache.releases.https) and snapshot repository (apache.snapshots.https). Credentials belong in the release manager's Maven settings, never in the repository.

The apache-release profile creates a buildable source archive and its SHA-512 checksum, attaches source and Javadoc jars, and signs artifacts with GPG. Normal builds include META-INF/LICENSE and META-INF/NOTICE in jars through the ASF resource bundle. The dependency-license report is written to target/DEPENDENCY-LICENSES; it is not a substitute for checking the contents of each distributed artifact.

Deployment is disabled in this branch's POM, including when apache-release is active. The release plugin runs verify and does not push SCM changes. CI has read-only repository permissions and does not publish artifacts. Enabling publication requires a separate reviewed build change.
Check release packaging locally without signing or uploading:

The unsigned source archive and checksum are written under the root target directory. These are test artifacts, not an Apache release. Before publication, a release manager must verify source completeness, dependency licenses, signatures, reproducibility, and compatibility with the selected core release. Staging and publication require the Apache Maven release procedure and an approved release vote under the ASF release policy.

section.title: Contributing
section.para: Use the OpenNLP contribution guide and discuss project-wide changes on the development mailing list.
An add-on that requires an API from an unmerged OpenNLP branch also needs the local core snapshot procedure.

section.title: Building against a local core snapshot
section.para: An add-on normally uses the OpenNLP version selected by the root opennlp.version property. A feature branch may temporarily override that property when its required API is still under OpenNLP review.
Use a local core build only when the required API is absent from the current OpenNLP release and Apache snapshot.

section.title: Use an isolated Maven repository
section.para: An isolated local repository prevents an experimental core build from replacing the regular OpenNLP snapshot in the default Maven cache. Set one absolute path and use it for both builds:
Build the exact OpenNLP feature branch:
section.screen: git clone https://github.com/apache/opennlp.git cd opennlp git fetch origin "$OPENNLP_CORE_REF" git switch --detach FETCH_HEAD ./mvnw install -DskipTests -Drat.skip=true -Dopennlp.forkCount=1 \ -Dmaven.repo.local="$OPENNLP_FEATURE_M2"
section.para: Use the same repository when verifying the add-on:
This procedure does not change artifacts in the default Maven cache. Remove the isolated directory when the local core build is no longer needed.

section.title: Return to the Apache snapshot
section.para: After the core PR merges and its snapshot is published, remove the module's temporary opennlp.version override. Verify with a fresh dependency lookup:
The add-on PR should compile against the published Apache artifacts before it is opened for review.
